newsitem.title: India: Silver, gold seized at India politician's homes.
newsitem.headline: Silver, gold seized at India politician's homes.

text.p: Police have seized half a tonne of silver in raids on the homes of India's best known woman politician who was arrested at the weekend in a corruption case, a police lawyer said on Monday.

"The police have recovered, among other things, half a tonne of silver and 30 to 40 kg (66 to 88 lb) of gold," N. Natarajan told a court in Madras after the raids, conducted over two days at two homes of Jayaram Jayalalitha in southern Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh states.
The lawyer said the seized bullion was worth 580 million rupees ($16.5 million).
Jayalalitha, a former movie star who ruled Tamil Nadu as chief minister, was arrested on Saturday, seven months after she was routed in regional elections.

The politician, whose regional party was an electoral ally of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's Congress party, has denied any wrongdoing and accused her successor government of victimising her.
More than 5,000 of her supporters were detained at the weekend after they launched violent protests against her arrest.
Police accused her of excess spending worth 85 million rupees ($2.4 million) on 45,302 television sets for villagers while she was chief minister.
Activists from Jayalalitha's All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) party were detained amid scattered incidents in the state, where film star politicians command a frenzied following.
One supporter set himself on fire to protest against Jayalalitha's arrest. He died the following day.
The United News of India (UNI) said police arrested two AIADMK activists in the city of Coimbatore when they tried to immolate themselves on Monday.

In Madurai town, police detained 68 party workers when they tried to picket trains and set up road blocks, the news agency said. Protests continued against the arrest of Jayalalitha in the state, it said.
Jayalalitha, 48, has been charged in seven corruption cases ranging from foreign exchange to income tax violations.
Lawmakers in the federal parliament sprang to her support on Monday, saying she was being mistreated in prison.

"This is a political persecution. Even a bathroom facility was given to her only for a limited time. The entire house condemns the maltreatment," said Sushma Swaraj, leader of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Jayalalitha spent her first night in Madras central jail sleeping on a bedsheet on the floor, news agencies said.

But they reported on Monday that she was allowed to meet visitors and provided with furniture, a mattress and newspapers following the local government's decision to accord her a higher status in the prison.
